title: NHS Trial at King's College London of Koa Health Foundations
content:
A landmark trial conducted at King's College London tested Koa Health Foundations — a digital mental health tool — with NHS staff. The trial investigated whether a structured digital intervention could meaningfully improve mental health outcomes in a high-pressure healthcare workforce.

Background

NHS staff face disproportionately high rates of stress, anxiety, and burnout. Traditional mental health support services often have long waiting lists or are underutilised due to stigma. Digital tools offer an opportunity to provide accessible, scalable, and proactive mental health support.

What Koa Foundations does

Koa Foundations is a clinically validated, evidence-based digital mental health platform built on cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) principles. It delivers structured programmes through a mobile app, designed to improve resilience and reduce symptoms of anxiety and depression.

Trial findings

The results of the trial showed promising improvements in participant mental health and wellbeing scores, supporting the case for wider deployment of digital mental health tools within the NHS workforce.
